items.caption: An oracle-bone form of 身, catalogued as 合822正, shows a person-like outline with a prominent marked midsection. Early interpretations differ on whether it depicts an abdomen or a pregnant figure.
items.alt: Black oracle-bone-style glyph with a slanting upper stroke, an enclosed oval midsection, and a long descending stroke.
items.selection_reason: This identified early form gives a useful visual anchor for the character’s history, while the evidence leaves its intended referent unresolved.

items.caption: A modern redraw of 身 in the small-seal style preserved in the Shuowen tradition, with a tall descending stroke and a rounded enclosure around the middle.
items.alt: Black seal-script glyph with an angled upper section, rounded central enclosure, and long vertical stroke below.
items.selection_reason: Provides a clearly identified later script form for comparison with the oracle-bone form; it does not establish a direct transformation between the two.

limitations.text: The oracle-bone figure’s marked midsection is interpreted either as an abdomen or as pregnancy; the surviving image does not settle which reading is correct. These redrawings also do not establish a complete dated sequence of graphic changes.
